music_drama_grammar.purpose: Formal grammar layer for Music Drama scenario writing. Defines structural rules and composition contracts without generating scenarios.

narrative_foundation.default_narrative_lens: protagonist POV — camera follows the active lead character's visual attention
narrative_foundation.emotional_arc_style: lyric-driven still moments with readable emotional residue between scenes

field_contract.absent_character_rule: omit only — never write exclusion phrases such as "No Dana" or "Dana absent"

density_limits.protagonist_dominance: crowd must never compete with protagonist visibility

continuity_grammar.companion_rule: companion animals remain present across adjacent scenes until departure is explicitly described in scenario
continuity_grammar.object_rule: held or carried objects persist until scenario explicitly removes them
continuity_grammar.weather_rule: time and weather must align with datasets/time/time-setting-library-v1.json

time_atmosphere_binding.rule: scenario atmosphere must not contradict selected timeSetting cluster

visual_anchor_grammar.purpose: recurring anchors improve image consistency across Music Drama scenes
visual_anchor_grammar.reuse_rule: prefer repeating compatible anchors within the same episode

pass_observations: character consistency improved with external manual scenario

known_risk_zones.mitigation: limit crowd groups and named extras per density_limits
keep bedding and body contact visually simple in domestic scenes
avoid complex hand poses in early test phases

shot_patterns.purpose: Reusable Music Drama shot-pattern grammar for still-image scenario composition. Patterns define framing intent only — not generated scenario text.

patterns.label: Establishing Daily Life
patterns.shot_role: open the viewer into a readable ordinary moment
patterns.framing_intent: wide-to-medium view of one primary location with protagonist clearly anchored
patterns.music_drama_function: lyric-aligned opening still that establishes emotional baseline

patterns.label: Companion Bond Moment
patterns.shot_role: show emotional readability through human-animal proximity
patterns.framing_intent: medium shot with protagonist and companion animal sharing frame space
scenario_field_focus: visible shared action between protagonist and companion
patterns.music_drama_function: quiet relationship beat supporting lyric warmth without dialogue exposition
patterns.rkb_note: RKB-001 validated Gamja companion stability in this pattern

patterns.label: Domestic Warmth
patterns.shot_role: express family comfort inside home or bakery interior
patterns.framing_intent: interior medium shot with warm domestic props and limited cast
patterns.music_drama_function: home-space emotional anchor for lyric passages about peace and belonging
patterns.risk_mitigation: avoid complex bedding geometry per RKB-001 object deformation finding

patterns.label: Bakery Morning
patterns.shot_role: anchor morning routine through bakery warmth and food preparation context
patterns.framing_intent: medium shot centered on bakery counter, oven glow, or window display
character_field_focus: optional queue extras as background only
patterns.music_drama_function: daily-life rhythm beat aligned with morning lyric sections

patterns.label: Harbor Edge Watch
patterns.shot_role: connect protagonist to sea, labor, and horizon without plot exposition
patterns.framing_intent: medium-wide shot with harbor elements and protagonist at rail, bench, or pier edge
character_field_focus: distant dock workers only if clearly visible
patterns.music_drama_function: horizon-gazing lyric still suggesting quiet future possibility

patterns.label: Street Passage
patterns.shot_role: move protagonist through village lanes with readable environment
patterns.framing_intent: tracking still of one lane or staircase with protagonist mid-passage
patterns.music_drama_function: transitional lyric still between domestic and harbor spaces

patterns.label: Quiet Solitude
patterns.shot_role: hold one emotionally readable solitary moment
patterns.framing_intent: medium close still with minimal background activity
patterns.music_drama_function: internal lyric pause rendered through environment and posture, not monologue

patterns.label: Rooftop Gaze
patterns.shot_role: elevated still looking over village roofline or wall boundary
patterns.framing_intent: medium-wide elevated view with protagonist at roof edge or high window
patterns.music_drama_function: lyric bridge about unchanged world and quiet curiosity

visibility_law.summary: Crowd exists to support world realism.
rules: Crowd must never dominate frame.
Crowd must never become primary subject.
Crowd must never compete with Gonegi.
Crowd remains background support for protagonist readability.

rkb_integration.market_crowd_caution: Use market groups sparingly; one crowd group maximum; keep Gonegi in clear foreground

living_world_crowd_alignment.note: Read-only alignment reference; does not modify Living World Core

groups.label: Market Vendors

animal_behavior.purpose: Animal and companion behavior grammar for Music Drama. Establishes companion hierarchy, animal continuity rules, background animal ecology, and living village atmosphere without generating scenarios.

section_1_primary_companion_layer.companion_hierarchy_rule: Primary companions always have higher priority than background animals.

companions.label: Gamja
companions.companion_continuity_law: If Gonegi appears, Gamja should appear unless physically impossible.

companions.label: Aengdu
companions.ep01_note: Reserved for post-EP01 Dana scenes; Dana does not appear in EP01
companions.companion_continuity_law: If Dana appears, Aengdu should appear unless physically impossible.

companion_continuity_law.gonegi_gamja: If Gonegi appears, Gamja should appear unless physically impossible.
companion_continuity_law.dana_aengdu: If Dana appears, Aengdu should appear unless physically impossible.
companion_continuity_law.priority: Primary companions outrank all background animals in character field ordering and visual emphasis.

section_3_background_animal_rotation_law.goal: Prevent the same background animal from appearing everywhere.
rules: Animals rotate naturally across environments.
No single background animal should dominate all scenes.
Select background animals from the environment-appropriate rotation zone only.
Do not stack multiple background animal types in one scene unless density law allows.

primary_companion.rule: One primary companion per protagonist in frame.

background_animals.rule: At most one background animal group per scene.

visible_animal_count.composition_rule: Primary companion + at most one background animal group + optional single background individual.

section_4_animal_density_law.protagonist_focus_rule: Animals must never replace protagonist focus.

rkb_findings.companion_lesson: Companion animals improve emotional readability and scene continuity
rkb_findings.animal_density_alignment: max 2 animals in grammar density_limits; recommended max 3 visible including companion

section_5_rkb_integration.alignment_with_daily_life_library: All 16 daily-life behaviors list gamja in continuity_companions

section_5_motif_continuity_law.purpose: Allow motifs to reappear across scenes to strengthen emotional memory.
rules: Motifs may persist as recurring visual anchors within an episode.
The same motif may reappear in different time states if continuity_capable is true.
Motif reappearance should support emotional memory, not create symbol clutter.
Scenario field carries motif presence through location, atmosphere, and visible environment.
Character field must not narrate motif meaning — visual presence only.

examples.effect: same window strengthens domestic emotional memory

section_6_motif_density_law.protagonist_readability_rule: Motifs support atmosphere; they must not compete with Gonegi or primary action.

grammar_alignment.field_separation: Motifs appear in scenario field context; character field remains visual identity only
grammar_alignment.persistent_object_rule: toast and carried objects follow continuity_state_law

emotional_transitions.purpose: Model emotional flow for Music Drama storytelling. Transition grammar only — no generated scenarios or prompts.

states.description: Ordinary calm and stable daily-life emotional baseline.
Family warmth, belonging, and domestic safety.
Gentle interest in the world beyond familiar routine.
Soft discovery and openness without plot shock.
Distance, desire, and emotional reach toward someone absent.
Forward-looking warmth; in EP01 expressed as quiet hope only.
Visible sorrow after loss, restriction, or separation event.
Emotional weight of something or someone gone.
Pain of being kept apart from a bonded person.
Restored connection after absence or crisis.
Quiet resolution after grief, memory loss, or fate.
Emotional residue of the past; unrecognized or recognized.

rules: Only use EP01-compatible motifs for EP01-compatible emotional states.
Future motifs remain future-only and link only to non-EP01 emotions.

section_5_emotional_continuity_law.summary: Emotion should not jump randomly between scenes.
not_recommended_examples: peace → extreme sadness without supported story event
rules: Prefer adjacent emotional transitions with plausibility score ≥ 0.85 within EP01.
Large emotional jumps require explicit story_stage support.
Transition plausibility_score ranges from 0.0 to 1.0.
EP01 scenes should remain within EP01-compatible emotional states.

grammar_alignment.field_separation: Emotional intent informs scenario atmosphere; character field remains visual identity only

beat_structure.purpose: Connect emotional transitions to musical structure for Music Drama. Beat grammar only — no generated scenarios or prompts.

alignment.crowd_density_caps: chorus and verse remain LOW crowd density for EP01

alignment.character_readability: camera_energy LOW-MEDIUM only; protagonist remains frame anchor

sequence_assembly.purpose: Define how Music Drama scenes assemble from beat through emotion, behavior, motif, shot pattern, archetype, and crowd/animal support. Assembly grammar only — no generated scenarios or prompts.

section_1_assembly_pipeline.pipeline_description: Each assembled scene slot is filled in this fixed order before Image App field conversion.

beats.motif_note: morning_light used as memory echo of intro beat

rules: Do not invent new emotional jumps.
Repeat compatible motifs across expanded scenes.
Preserve continuity companion across adjacent scenes.
Preserve protagonist readability in every expanded slot.
Expansion inserts intermediate scenes between beats using allowed emotional transitions only.
Each expanded scene must complete the full assembly pipeline in section_1 order.
section_3_scene_count_expansion_rule.expansion_method: subdivide beats with compatible daily-life behaviors and matching shot/archetype pairs from existing grammar libraries

companion_rules.gonegi_gamja: Gamja persists with Gonegi across adjacent EP01 scenes unless departure is explicitly described.
companion_rules.dana_aengdu: Aengdu persists with Dana only when Dana appears in future episodes.

section_4_continuity_state_transfer.object_rule: Carried objects such as toast persist until scenario explicitly removes them.
section_4_continuity_state_transfer.location_anchor_rule: Recurring anchors such as window and harbor_bench may reappear to strengthen motif continuity.
section_4_continuity_state_transfer.time_cluster_rule: Time atmosphere must stay compatible with datasets/time/time-setting-library-v1.json

mitigations.blanket_body_merge: Prefer simple bedding in domestic_bedroom_peace and night_rest beats
